verdict.rationale: Lambda documents that every On-Demand Cloud instance ships a preinstalled JupyterLab server, opened from the Instances page in the console. That delivers the story's 'open Jupyter in one step' path, and a community user describes working in Jupyter on a Lambda instance. Developers otherwise connect over SSH using console-managed keys; there is no first-party VS Code or Cursor integration. missing for 10: documented one-click IDE (VS Code/Cursor) connect flow, detailed docs on the JupyterLab launch steps and authentication.

support.subject: As a developer, I can open Jupyter or connect my IDE (VS Code/Cursor) to the instance in one step

citations.quote: each ODC instance provides a JupyterLab installation for creating and managing Jupyter notebooks. You can access your instance's JupyterLab by visiting the Instances page
You can connect to your On-Demand Cloud (ODC) instances directly through SSH or by using the preinstalled JupyterLab server.
You can import an existing key if you have one, or you can generate a new one in the Lambda Cloud console.
